articles.title: What's going on with Jalen Hurts' blood clots? Medical experts explain what the Eagles' QB is battling — and how long his recovery will take
articles.summary: What exactly is Hurts experiencing and what does it mean for his short- and long-term health?
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles have placed starting quarterback Jalen Hurts on injured reserve after a blood clot moved deeper into Hurts' calf and then spread to his lungs, per a team statement.

Hurts' diagnosis has shifted rapidly — from doctors discovering a superficial blood clot in his calf on Saturday, Oct. 10 to Hurts playing the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Oct. 11 to doctors discovering movement in the clot on Oct. 14.

By Oct. 15, last Thursday, Hurts was ruled out for the weekend . By Saturday, he was placed on the minimum-four-week injured reserve. And on Monday, the Eagles announced that Hurts' blood clot had not just moved to the deep veins of his calf but also reached his lungs — a dramatic swing from the initial injury that didn't restrict Hurts' clearance to play or travel.

What exactly is the Eagles quarterback experiencing and what does it mean for his short- and long-term health? Yahoo Sports spoke to two medical experts to better understand.

Dr. Ben Levine is a professor of internal medicine at UT Southwestern and director of the Institute for Exercise and Environmental Medicine, a collaboration between UT Southwestern and Texas Health Presbyterian Hospital Dallas. Dr. Thomas Maldonado is a professor of vascular surgery at the NYU Grossman School of Medicine.

Neither physician has worked with Hurts directly. Each spoke by phone generally about their experience studying and treating patients with blood clots, including Levine's experience studying clinical considerations for competitive athletes diagnosed with blood clots .

Here's some of what we learned from their guidance:

What is the difference between Hurts' initial diagnosis and his current one?

Doctors in London initially diagnosed Hurts with a superficial blood clot, the Eagles said in a Thursday statement. That constitutes a blood clot closer to the skin and above the fascia, a layer of tissue. Back in Philadelphia, Hurts' diagnosis was updated to a deep vein clot (clinically a deep vein "thrombosis") which spread to both of Hurts' lungs ("bilateral pulmonary emboli," as the Eagles and Hurts' agent Nicole Lynn said in a statement). How does one become the other?

"In this particular case, there was a component in the deep system, whether that was there at the get-go or whether that resulted because the clot in the superficial vein spilled into the deep vein," Maldonado said. "These veins connect usually up in the groin or sometimes behind the knee, the superficial and the deep connect and come together. And sometimes if there's a clot very close to that connection or junction, then that can spill into the deep system and that's very likely what happened here."

Clots that travel to the lungs can block or clog an artery, and in severe cases be fatal, Maldonado said. Larger clots are at greater risk of clogging arteries and triggering fatalities. The Eagles' statement that Hurts is "clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations" suggests those more severe outcomes, at this point, have been avoided.

This might feel like an obvious question, but the answer is less obvious. The blood clot itself is not what's keeping Hurts from playing. Rather, the blood-thinning medication ("anticoagulation," clinically) is keeping him from playing football. Superficial blood clots are not typically treated with blood thinners, Levine and Maldonado said. Once the clot was found to have moved deeper — and, now, to the lungs — blood thinners become the treatment plan and the hindrance to football. The risk of bleeding from a contact injury and then not clotting while on the blood-thinning medication is too high.

"You give an anticoagulant to protect the veins from getting more blood clots and to prevent even more blood clots from breaking off and flowing into the lungs …" Levine said. "Sports where collision is part and parcel of the game … you can imagine that if you're giving a blood thinner to prevent blood clotting, that if you got hit hard in the head, for example, you might get a hemorrhage or blood bleeding into your brain or into another part of your body, which wouldn't be so good. So those are conditions where you would be pretty cautious and concerned about someone who's on a blood thinner playing that sport."

Again, neither of these physicians have treated Hurts. But each agreed that the typical recovery timeline on blood-thinners after a clot moves into deep veins and lungs is three to six months. An ultrasound at three months could determine whether the clots have "healed" or dissipated. Hurts' age (28) plays to his favor as does his seeming ability to determine what triggered these clots: Hurts was kicked in the calf with a cleat on Oct. 4, a local trauma that could produce a clot. He also flew from Philadelphia to London and back for the game, a roughly seven-plus hour flight each way. Long flights, and particularly the immobility and/or dehydration that can come with flights, can provoke clots.

"If you know and can clearly see when it happened and why, typically the recommendations are the wiggle room is three to six months," Levine said. "I think even the most liberal doctors who manage these conditions would want to make sure that someone was fully anti-coagulated for at least three months. … If it's a clear, provoked event, and you can document that the vein is opened and that they're in the leg, for example, if that's where it occurred, that there's good blood flow, that there's no further evidence of unresolved blood clots in the lung, that the right ventricle [the lower right chamber of the heart] is functioning normally, then at three months you can start to have that discussion."

The Eagles and Lynn said in their statement that Hurts' "prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery," including the return to contact football once off blood thinners.

Could the long flights to play internationally have contributed to Hurts' diagnosis?

It's impossible for doctors who haven't examined Hurts to determine which risk factor triggered Hurts. But "long plane rides are notorious for increasing the risk of having a blood clot in the leg because you're stuck," Levine said, "and for big people like American football players, even a first-class seat can be pretty tight. So you're stuck and you can't move and you're very still and you're not moving your muscles. When you contract your muscles, that pushes the blood back to the heart and keeps the blood moving. But if your legs are pointed down and you're stuck there in a tight spot, it increases the risk of what we call stasis. That means the blood's not moving through the veins."

Immobility, in particular, is the concern on flights given how calf contractions help move blood back to the heart and reduce the chance of clotting.

"That's why people who have long plane travel, sometimes we encourage them to get up, stretch their legs, walk around, stay hydrated, avoid things like alcohol or caffeine that can dehydrate you on a plane," Maldonado said. "Compression stocking sometimes people wear on a plane to help give external support and prevent blood from pooling in the calves. Flexing your heels, 'pumping the gas,' so to speak — getting that calf muscle working."

The NFLPA sent a travel kit to all players on teams playing international games, a union spokesperson told Yahoo Sports. The kit included Firefly recovery devices designed to improve blood circulation and EXOS travel exercises.

Is it unusual for a superficial blood clot to become a deep blood clot?

Each doctor confirmed that most superficial blood clots, such as the clot that forms in a vein after receiving an IV or giving blood, do not enter the deep vein nor travel beyond.

Levine described the transition of a clot from superficial to deep as "very rare," while Maldonado noted that by definition, Hurts had a deep clot at some point.

"Whether it was a superficial clot that then as a result of this sort of setting propagated into the deep system or whether it was really both a superficial and deep clot is hard to say, but it's that combination of the perfect storm of being on a long plane trip, [possibly] dehydrated, et cetera, immobile that" could cause this, Maldonado said. "In the superficial clot that he developed, it's very unusual for it to result in this scenario where it's gone to the lungs. But now that it's gone to the lungs, now they're going to treat this as a much more unstable situation where they want to make sure he doesn't have other blood clots going to the lungs."

In the interim, Hurts can and will remain around the team conditioning in non-contact ways, the Eagles and Lynn said in the statement.

"We anticipate that he will have no long-term effects," the statement said. "We are thinking of Jalen and looking forward to a strong recovery."

articles.title: Cris Collinsworth Forced to Apologize on Live TV After Leaking Private Mike Tirico Conversation
articles.summary: In 2017, Tony Romo walked off the field as a Dallas Cowboys quarterback and straight into the CBS booth. Within weeks, he was being praised for calling plays...
articles.body:
In 2017, Tony Romo walked off the field as a Dallas Cowboys quarterback and straight into the CBS booth. Within weeks, he was being praised for calling plays before they happened. The sports world learned something that year: the best analysts aren't always the ones who prepared for the job. They're the ones who say what they're thinking. On Sunday night, Cris Collinsworth brought that same idea to a live NBC broadcast when he revealed that he and Mike Tirico had spent time debating the same role for Aaron Rodgers.

The conversation took place before the final minutes of the Dallas Cowboys vs. Green Bay Packers game at Lambeau Field on October 18, where Collinsworth decided a private dinner was too good to keep private.

"The bottom line is, like I always thought that John McEnroe, when he was a tennis announcer, you knew from what he said as a player, like he didn't withhold anything, right? Officials and whatever, he was gonna let you know exactly what he felt, which is great for a broadcaster, and I think Aaron would fall into that same category," Collinsworth said [ h/t: Awful Announcing ]. "We know at the very least we're gonna know what he's thinking."

However, that conversation was not supposed to go public. Tirico confirmed this when he said, "That was supposed to stay at dinner."

Collinsworth agreed and apologized quickly.

As a player, John McEnroe was fiery and blunt. When he transitioned to the booth for networks like NBC Sports and ESPN, he maintained that exact persona. He did not filter his thoughts to protect players' feelings or bow to decorum, offering blunt critiques of officials, players, and tennis schedules.

Collinsworth's comparison hinged entirely on this trait. Aaron Rodgers is highly vocal and completely unfiltered as well. Most recently, during the Week 4 clash against the Cleveland Browns, the Pittsburgh Steelers QB was caught shouting expletives at the sideline regarding play-calling to head coach Mike McCarthy and staff.

Other than that, there is one more possible explanation behind Cris Collinsworth and Mike Tirico's discussion and comparison of Aaron Rodgers with John McEnroe.

McEnroe transitioned almost immediately toward the end of his playing days, starting with NBC in 1992. Meanwhile, Rodgers has confirmed the 2026 season as his final year as a player in the NFL.

Now, with CBS parting ways with its long-time lead analyst, Tony Romo, and Troy Aikman nearing his contract expiration with ESPN after Super Bowl LXI in February 2027, Rodgers might become a hot prospect for many broadcasting networks.

However, the 42-year-old Steelers QB has blatantly disregarded the idea of transitioning into sports media following his NFL retirement.

"When this is done, it's Keyser Söze," Rodgers said on The Pat McAfee Show in March 2026. "You won't see me. I'm not doing TV. I'm not going to be out and about."

While Cris Collinsworth loves the idea of Aaron Rodgers in a booth as an NFL analyst, the Steelers QB remains focused on the task at hand to lead his franchise to a triumphant season in his final year.

articles.title: Jay-Z Looks To Have Picked Jay-Z To Headline 2027 Super Bowl Halftime Show
articles.summary: Jay-Z, whose Roc Nation is the organizer behind the Apple Music Super Bowl Halftime Show, will be the headliner for the 2027 event at Los Angeles’ SoFi Stadi...
articles.body:
Jay-Z, whose Roc Nation is the organizer behind the Apple Music Super Bowl Halftime Show, will be the headliner for the 2027 event at Los Angeles' SoFi Stadium, a music industry insider has confirmed to Deadline.

The rap superstar and 25-time Grammy winner has been in the news amidst his global Jay-Z 30 Tour concerts to commemorate the 30th anniversary of his debut album Reasonable Doubt and the 25th anniversary of his seminal The Blueprint . As part of those milestones, an eight-part docuseries Jay-Z in 8 about his career, done in conversation with uber-producer Rick Rubin, launched on HBO Max and HBO last month.

This 2027 Super Bowl is set for February 14 at SoFi, the Inglewood venue where Jay-Z is playing two shows this Friday and Saturday – likely the perfect place to make it official he will be back for Super Bowl halftime duties. ESPN is airing this year's game which will be simulcast on ABC.

The NFL did not respond to a request for comment on the Jay-Z news Tuesday.

With Jay-Z set, the next question would be who will join him as special guests. Beyoncé is a likely pick (she appeared during the Yankee Stadium leg of the tour with her spouse), with others including Nas and Pharrell Williams also part of the NYC shows. The recent London leg at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium featured a mini-Fugees reunion with Lauryn Hill and Wyclef.

Another possibility: In May, Jay-Z joined his longtime collaborators The Roots to headline the band's Roots Picnic in Philadelphia, their first get-together in more than a decade.

Last year, Bad Bunny was the headliner at the Super Bowl Halftime Show at Levis Stadium in San Francisco. The performance, which featured appearances by Lady Gaga and Ricky Martin and cameos from Jessica Alba, Pedro Pascal and more, drew 128.8 million viewers. That was down slightly from Kendrick Lamar's record-setting 133M viewer total in 2025.

Lamar co-headlined the 2022 halftime show, the last time the Super Bowl was in L.A. He was joined by Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg, Eminem and Mary J. Blige for that performance.

Puck was the first to report Jay-Z's selection.

articles.title: Travis Kelce eyes another Pennsylvania estate amid growing neighbour tensions over $5.35 million Ohio mansion
articles.summary: Travis Kelce has spent years building his life around football, but retirement could bring a major change to his plans.
articles.body: Travis Kelce has spent years building his life around football, but retirement could bring a major change to his plans. The Kansas City Chiefs star has several properties to consider as he looks beyond his NFL career. Reports of a possible private estate in Pennsylvania have added another twist to the story, while a dispute surrounding his Ohio mansion has raised questions about where he and Taylor Swift might settle down. Kelce has yet to reveal his long-term plans, leaving fans to wonder whether Kansas City will remain his home after football.Travis Kelce’s reported Pennsylvania estate adds to retirement speculationKelce’s future away from the field remains uncertain, but reports of a possible Pennsylvania estate have drawn fresh attention to his property investments. According to Deuxmoi, sources claim that Kelce and Swift purchased several properties in the state over the past few years and may be combining them into a larger private estate.Construction is reportedly underway, with privacy said to be a key priority. However, neither Kelce nor Swift has confirmed the reported purchases or building plans.Other rumors have linked the couple to properties in Montana, Utah and Carmel, California. Reports have also mentioned possible acquisitions in Florida and the Bahamas, although these claims remain unconfirmed.For Kelce, such properties could offer options once he steps away from the demands of professional football. The veteran tight end has spent most of his career in Kansas City, where his football commitments have shaped his daily routine. Retirement could give him more freedom to choose where he wants to spend his time.Still, there is no confirmed timeline for his departure from the NFL or any announcement about his next permanent home.Travis Kelce’s Ohio mansion faces a neighborhood disputeKelce’s reported real estate plans also come amid a dispute involving a 21,000-square-foot mansion in Bratenahl, Ohio. The property, reportedly worth around $5.34 million, has become a point of disagreement with nearby residents over plans for a six-foot fence and tree planting near an old clay sewer line.According to Star Magazine, the disagreement has reportedly upset the couple, who hoped to maintain good relations with their neighbors.“The last thing they wanted was to have any sort of friction with their neighbors [and] have tried so hard to make sure people would be happy,” a source told the publication.The insider also claimed that the couple had covered expenses that neighbors might otherwise have shared. The source suggested they could consider selling the property if tensions continue, though no sale has been confirmed.Meanwhile, Kansas City remains an important option for Kelce. He owns a roughly 17,000-square-foot mansion in Leawood, Kansas, with a pool, tennis court, media lounge and other luxury features. The garden also holds special meaning because Kelce reportedly proposed there.For now, the Chiefs star has offered no public confirmation of his post-NFL living arrangements. articles.title: "Screwed up a lot as a parent": Tom Brady reflects on parenting mistakes and admits raising three kids has not always been easy
articles.summary: Tom Brady spent more than two decades proving himself on the football field, but fatherhood has taught him lessons no Super Bowl victory could prepare him
articles.body: Tom Brady spent more than two decades proving himself on the football field, but fatherhood has taught him lessons no Super Bowl victory could prepare him for. Looking back at a candid interview from October 2024, the retired NFL quarterback spoke honestly about the challenges his three children face while growing up with a famous father. Brady also admitted that he has made mistakes as a parent. His comments offered a rare glimpse into his family life and showed how he wants his children to chase their own dreams, even when the odds seem stacked against them.Tom Brady opens up about parenting challenges and his children's futureDuring an appearance at the Fortune Global Forum in New York City in October 2024, Brady reflected on how his football legacy could affect his children. The seven-time Super Bowl champion shares son Jack, now 17 at the time of the interview, with Bridget Moynahan. He also has Benjamin and Vivian with his ex-wife, Gisele Bündchen.Brady acknowledged that being his son could come with its own set of pressures, especially for a boy trying to build an identity outside his father's achievements."To be a boy, [it] s*cks to be Tom Brady's son in so many ways," he said, per Us Weekly. "There's a lot of challenges I faced as a kid … my kids naturally are gonna be faced with their own challenges, and they gotta figure out how to overcome them. I'll be there to support them and I'll be learning along the way with them."Rather than expecting his children to follow in his footsteps, Brady said he wanted to help them find their own paths. Jack, for instance, hoped to become a basketball player, despite not having the same jumping ability as his father might wish."Unfortunately, he jumps as high as I do."Brady's response was to encourage his son's ambition instead of discouraging him because of his current limitations.Tom Brady reveals the parenting lesson he learned from his parentsBrady credited his own parents for giving him the freedom to pursue football when success was far from guaranteed. He recalled being a backup quarterback on his freshman team and said they never pushed him to abandon his ambitions."Whatever our kids choose … we gotta support [them]," Brady said. "The blessings my parents gave me was when I was that long shot as a kid who was a backup quarterback on a freshman team … they never said, 'Man, don't do that. It's gonna be too hard. Let's do something different. Let's think about another backup plan.' They kind of said, 'You know what, go for it. Whatever you wanna be, go for it.' And that's probably my parenting style."He wanted Jack to feel the same confidence, telling him, "Dude, you're gonna be a stud." Brady added, "Wait till you hit your growth spurt, you're gonna be jumping higher, you're gonna be dunking."The former quarterback also acknowledged his shortcomings, admitting that he had "screwed up a lot as a parent" while trying to remain dependable and consistent.In August 2024, Brady celebrated Jack's 17th birthday with a heartfelt Instagram message, praising his son's kindness, dedication and love for family. He also joked that Jack could now beat him in one-on-one basketball.Looking back, Brady's comments showed a different side of the NFL legend. His record on the field may be extraordinary, but his approach to fatherhood rests on something simpler: supporting his children, accepting his mistakes and letting them discover who they want to become.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Chiefs owners’  $900,000 political donations revealed as the $15 billion Hunt family backs conservative causes
articles.summary: Last year, as the Kansas City Chiefs prepared to face the Philadelphia Eagles in Super Bowl 59, attention turned to a side of the franchise that rarely
articles.body: Last year, as the Kansas City Chiefs prepared to face the Philadelphia Eagles in Super Bowl 59, attention turned to a side of the franchise that rarely dominated game-day discussions. While Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce stayed away from presidential endorsements, the Chiefs’ ownership had a different record on political involvement. Reports highlighted the Hunt family’s donations to conservative causes, its religious and pro-life positions, and questions about the treatment of players within the organisation.Chiefs owners’ political donations revealed the Hunt family’s conservative tiesIn February 2025, a report by The Spun examined the political activity of the Hunt family, which owns the Kansas City Chiefs. The family, led by owner Clark Hunt, had largely kept political matters separate from the team’s public image, but its financial contributions told another story.According to NBC News, the Hunt family, valued at more than $15 billion by Forbes at the time, had donated approximately $900,000 to candidates and committees over the previous decade. The report said those contributions went almost exclusively to conservative causes, based on federal and state filings.Norma Hunt, the family matriarch, had contributed nearly $500,000 to federal campaigns since 2016. Clark Hunt, who serves as the Chiefs’ CEO, had donated more than $200,000 to federal campaigns over the same period.The family had also supported conservative positions on religious matters and pro-life causes. These contributions offered a clearer picture of the owners’ political leanings, even as the team’s most recognisable figures avoided publicly backing a presidential candidate before the 2024 election.Mahomes and Kelce both chose not to endorse a candidate. Their approach kept the focus on football rather than party politics, a distinction that became more noticeable as the franchise attracted national attention during its Super Bowl run.Chiefs ownership faced player treatment criticism amid Super Bowl successThe Hunt family’s political activity was not the only issue surrounding the Chiefs’ ownership last year. The franchise also faced criticism over its workplace conditions and support staff.In an anonymous player survey, the Chiefs’ ownership received an “F” grade. The team also received failing marks for its locker room, nutritionist and training staff, raising questions about the experience of players away from the spotlight.Those findings offered a contrast to Kansas City’s success on the field. Under head coach Andy Reid and quarterback Patrick Mahomes, the Chiefs had established themselves as one of the NFL’s leading teams, winning three Super Bowls during their dominant run.Ahead of Super Bowl 59 on February 9, 2025, Kansas City aimed to become the first team to win three consecutive Super Bowl titles. The Eagles ultimately beat the Chiefs 40-22, ending that bid.The political donations and player survey brought attention to the people running the franchise, not just the stars wearing its uniform. While the Chiefs continued to draw praise for their football achievements, the reports showed that ownership decisions and off-field concerns remained part of the wider conversation about the organisation.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Travis Kelce's heartbreak deepens as $1.7 billion Cleveland Guardians extend World Series drought to 78 years
articles.summary: The Cleveland Guardians have suffered another painful postseason exit, extending a championship drought that has haunted the city for nearly eight decades.
articles.body: The Cleveland Guardians have suffered another painful postseason exit, extending a championship drought that has haunted the city for nearly eight decades. Their 7-3 defeat to the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 6 of the American League Championship Series ended their hopes of reaching the 2026 World Series. For fans, including Kansas City Chiefs star Travis Kelce, the loss brings another reminder of Cleveland’s long wait for baseball glory. The Rays, meanwhile, secured their place in the Fall Classic, where they will face the Milwaukee Brewers in a matchup between two teams chasing their first World Series championship.Cleveland Guardians fall short after promising ALCS startCleveland looked well placed to reach the World Series after winning two of the first three games against Tampa Bay. However, the Guardians could not maintain that momentum as the Rays won three consecutive games to close out the series.The decisive Game 6 exposed Cleveland's struggles at the plate and the pressure on its pitching staff. Tampa Bay built an early advantage and controlled much of the contest, leaving the Guardians searching for a response.Junior Caminero delivered a crucial blow in the seventh inning when he launched a two-run homer off Cleveland closer Cade Smith. Yandy Díaz added another two-run home run in the eighth, giving Tampa Bay a cushion that proved decisive.Cleveland made a late push in the eighth inning, cutting the deficit from four runs to two after a series of walks and a hit batter brought home two runs. Yet the rally ended when Kevin Kelly struck out Brayan Rocchio with the bases loaded.The defeat was especially frustrating for a Guardians team that led the American League with 41 comeback victories during the regular season. Their inability to take control in the closing stages of the series ultimately proved costly.Travis Kelce and Cleveland fans face another championship heartbreakCleveland's latest elimination extends its World Series title drought to 78 years. The franchise last won the championship in 1948, when it defeated the Boston Braves. Although the team has reached the World Series four times since then, it has yet to bring another title home.For Cleveland supporters, the latest setback adds another chapter to a long history of postseason disappointment. The Guardians won the AL Central and advanced past the Chicago White Sox in the Division Series, raising hopes that this could finally be their year.Manager Stephen Vogt acknowledged the disappointment after the loss.“Yeah, let it hurt,” Cleveland manager Stephen Vogt said he told his club. “That hurts. I couldn’t be more proud of our group. It just hurts. It stings. Really felt like we had a team to go and just weren’t able to get there.”The Guardians now face an offseason of reflection after coming so close to the biggest stage in baseball.For the Rays, the victory brings a different opportunity. They will meet the Milwaukee Brewers in a World Series featuring two franchises still searching for their first championship. While Tampa Bay prepares for that historic contest, Cleveland must wait another year to chase the title that has eluded the city since 1948.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Brittany Mahomes has found herself at the centre of another social media storm after sharing new photos from her Adidas campaign.
articles.body: Brittany Mahomes has found herself at the centre of another social media storm after sharing new photos from her Adidas campaign. The wife of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes showed off her fitness in the shoot, but the response quickly turned personal. While some followers praised her appearance and dedication to staying fit as a mother of three, others used the comments to criticise her lifestyle and past public controversies. The reaction grew intense enough for Brittany to limit comments on Instagram, bringing fresh attention to the challenges she faces as a high-profile NFL wife.Brittany Mahomes faces backlash over her latest Adidas photoshootBrittany's partnership with Adidas reflects her background as a former college athlete and her continued interest in fitness. Her latest Instagram carousel featured a sportswear campaign that highlighted her physique and active lifestyle.Several followers responded positively, with one writing, “Beautiful and stunning so hard to believe your a mom of 3”However, the post also attracted personal remarks. One commenter took a swipe at her appearance, writing, “She got them implants so he don’t stray!!!”The criticism went beyond the photos themselves. Discussions on Reddit focused on Brittany's public image, with some users arguing that her online behaviour had contributed to the negative attention she receives.“My thing with her is that she’s had chances to improve her image. People already started to dislike her when she sprayed champagne on those fans. And instead of apologizing, she clap-backs in a childish way. Then she was able to redeem herself on the QB show because Patrick film crew made sure to give her a nice edit. Then she shows herself again by defending Jackson,” a comment reads.“Then she was able to get redeemed again because Taylor liked hanging with her. But she shows her a– again by liking that maga post. And instead of clearing it up, she goes and posts a clap back again. She has nobody to blame but herself. The internet now knows your digital footprint.”The comments show how quickly a fitness post can become a wider debate when a celebrity already attracts strong opinions online. However, the harsh remarks remain the views of individual users, rather than evidence of how the public as a whole feels about Brittany.Patrick Mahomes' wife faces renewed scrutiny over her public imageBrittany's lifestyle has also become a point of discussion among critics who believe she shares too much of her personal life online.One Reddit user expressed frustration with what they viewed as her tendency to show off her wealth and lifestyle.“For me, it’s her constant bragging. Most ‘influencers’ do it. What ever happened to moms teaching their kids they shouldn’t brag? BM is shameless, materialistic, and promoting all the wrong values, IMO,” they wrote.Another commenter suggested that her approach to social media contributes to the repeated criticism.“If she would just sit the f–k down, this wouldn’t be a thing. Being thirsty has its disadvantages,” they shared.Not everyone joined in the criticism. Some users on the same discussion forum expressed sympathy for the level of hostility directed at her, even when they disagreed with her past actions.For Brittany, the latest episode highlights the difficult balance between maintaining a public profile and dealing with online abuse. As the wife of one of the NFL's biggest stars, her posts often attract attention far beyond the original content.Limiting Instagram comments may help reduce some of the immediate negativity, but the episode shows how her public image continues to fuel debate among football fans and celebrity followers.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "Life could change at a blink of an eye": Jalen Hurts’ mother Pamela shares heartbreaking message as Eagles QB faces serious health scare
articles.summary: Jalen Hurts’ health has become a major concern for Philadelphia Eagles fans, but a message from his mother, Pamela, has offered a deeply personal glimpse
articles.body: Jalen Hurts’ health has become a major concern for Philadelphia Eagles fans, but a message from his mother, Pamela, has offered a deeply personal glimpse into what the family may be going through. As the quarterback faces a serious blood clot issue that has reportedly ended his 2026 season, Pamela turned to TikTok with a reminder about how quickly life can change. Her words did not directly address her son’s condition, yet the timing gave the message added weight. For fans watching the situation unfold, her call to appreciate life struck a powerful chord.Pamela Hurts shares an emotional message amid Jalen Hurts’ health scarePamela posted a video on TikTok on Tuesday, with the recording showing the floor as she spoke. Eagles Nation and the New York Post shared the message, which appeared to be her first public response amid the growing attention surrounding her son’s health.“Just a reminder, y’all: be grateful," Pamela said. "Be grateful for where you are and what you have because your life could change at a blink of an eye. Be grateful. What are you grateful for?”The message carried a simple but powerful point. Health and everyday life can change without warning, leaving little time to prepare for what comes next. Although Pamela did not name Jalen or discuss his medical condition, the circumstances surrounding the post made her words especially meaningful to concerned fans.Hurts, 28, has reportedly been placed on injured reserve because of the blood clot issue and is not expected to return this season. articles.title: ‘There must be a full investigation’: Players union refuses to move on from Jalen Hurts situation
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles have faced plenty of questions over how they handled star quarterback Jalen Hurts’ blood clot, which went undisclosed as he traveled...
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles have faced plenty of questions over how they handled star quarterback Jalen Hurts' blood clot, which went undisclosed as he traveled to London, played against the Jacksonville Jaguars, and flew back home. The NFL appears ready to move on from the situation, but the players' union isn't.

On Tuesday night, the NFL Players Association released a statement calling for a "full investigation" into the medical care Hurts received. The union also revealed that the league had told it that it did not plan to review the situation.

Hurts sought treatment on his calf on Oct. 8 before the Eagles flew to London. He was listed with a calf injury on the injury report but was a full participant in practice.

On Oct. 10, a superficial blood clot was found in his left calf during a visit to the Cleveland Clinic in London. Hurts was cleared to play the next day and played the entire game in the Eagles' 19-17 loss to the Jaguars before flying home with the team that night.

A follow-up ultrasound on Oct. 14 revealed that the clot had moved, and Hurts was eventually placed on injured reserve. Then on Monday, the Eagles announced that his diagnosis had been updated to deep vein thrombosis "as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli," meaning there were now clots in both of his lungs.

The team said that Hurts' prognosis is "very good," but he's expected to miss the rest of the season while on blood thinners.

Despite the questions surrounding the situation, the NFL has concluded that the process that led to Hurts being cleared to play in London "was handled appropriately," according to The Athletic . The league will not punish the Eagles.

The NFL also released a statement on Tuesday, saying it had been in contact with the Eagles' medical staff and the Cleveland Clinic throughout the process.

While the NFL might be looking to move on from the situation, NFLPA isn't ready to do that just yet. In fact, the union is demanding a "full investigation" into the matter.

"The NFLPA is not aware of any NFL investigation into the medical care provided to Jalen Hurts," the union said in a statement, via Pro Football Talk . "In fact, the league previously informed the union that it did not plan to review the care he received."

"Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred," the statement continued. "Determining the facts is essential to ensuring players receive the highest level of care and protection going forward."

We'll have to see whether or not the league does decide

articles.title: Allen Sills dismisses concern about team physician bias as "nonsense" (it's not)
articles.summary: When it comes to whether the Eagles properly handled the health care provided to Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts for his blood clots, the NFL is hardly a neut...
articles.body:
When it comes to whether the Eagles properly handled the health care provided to Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts for his blood clots, the NFL is hardly a neutral, disinterested party. It was the NFL, through chief medical officer Allen Sills, that arranged for the evaluation of Hurts in London, which is part of what the league does to support all NFL teams that are imposed upon to play internationally.

On Tuesday, Sills spoke to reporters at the quarterly ownership meeting in New York. And he arguably protested too much when it comes to lingering concerns about the NFL's culture regarding medical care for players.

"Any idea or any suggestion that a team physician is ever being influenced by a coach, a General Manager, a team owner — it just doesn't happen," Sills insisted. "There is no doctor who is taking orders from a football person, a non-medical person. Period."

Setting aside whether he's directly aware of how all 32 teams operate (he surely isn't), in this context an express order isn't needed. Team-hired doctors understand the assignment; the teams want players to be available to play. In nearly every case, the player wants to be available, too. Any doctor who develops a reputation in the building for being unnecessarily cautious when it comes to clearing a player to play will inevitably be replaced by a doctor who will.

And those assignments are very lucrative, both in what they pay to the doctor and in how they provide the doctor with built-in marketing for the rest of the doctor's practice.

"The notion that there are external factors or that any of our physicians would put a player in harm's way, that's nonsense," Sills said.

The dismissal of that possibility does not mesh with the facts. The mere existence of the Unaffiliated Neurotrauma Consultant program for diagnosing concussions and clearing players to return from concussions directly refutes Sills's contention. If team doctors could be relied upon in every instance to set aside the unspoken (because it doesn't need to be said) urgency to find that a potentially concussed player is good to go or to clear a concussed player to return, there would be NO NEED for doctors with no team affiliation.

As to most other health issues, the situation isn't as critical. Orthopedic injuries don't put a player at risk, and a shot or two of Toradol never hurt anyone, right? (Well, maybe not .)

In those rare instances where the shared desire for the team and the player to "be available" intersects with the player's best interests as a patient, there's inherent pressure on the team-hired doctor to get along by going along.

It's unfortunate that Sills refused to recognize this basic fact. Hopefully, he said it for P.R. purposes and not because he truly believes it.

Finally, Sills invoked "patient privacy concerns" to justify not taking questions about the treatment Hurts received. That's a copout. Hurts has already authorized the issuance of multiple statements that shared with the world various details about his private medical issues.

It's easy to use "patient privacy concerns" as a shield when, in reality, the player quite possibly would authorize doctors to answer any and all questions about a situation that has already become extremely public. At this point, why would Hurts object to his doctors explaining what they did and why they did it?

Through it all, the NFL and the Eagles simply want to move on. All's well that ends, as the late NFL Commissioner Paul Tagliabue liked to say. Hopefully, this one won't end until all necessary questions are asked and answered — and until the NFL recognizes that, for certain health conditions, a UNC-style approach is needed.

articles.title: NFL chief medical officer: Eagles' approach to Hurts was 'appropriately guarded'
articles.summary: L officials Tuesday staunchly defended the medical process involving Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts' blood clot issue.
articles.body:
NFL officials Tuesday staunchly defended the medical process involving Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts' blood clot issue.

NFL chief medical officer Allen Sills was blunt in a news conference from the owners meetings.

"The notion that there's external factors that any of our physicians would put a player in harm's way -- that's nonsense," Sills said.

The NFL is not punishing the Eagles for the handling of Hurts, who was cleared to play before Week 5 against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London's Tottenham Hotspur Stadium after he was initially diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in his calf.

Hurts, 28, is expected to miss the rest of the season after doctors discovered multiple blood clots in the quarterback's lungs days after the game. Hurts will undergo treatment involving blood thinners that is expected to sideline the three-time Pro Bowler for around three months.

Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, and the Eagles released a statement Monday detailing Hurts' condition. Lynn and the Eagles said Hurts has deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, meaning a blood clot traveled from his legs to his lungs.

NFL officials confirmed Tuesday that it had been in contact with Eagles medical personnel and Cleveland Clinic London throughout the process of Hurts being treated. Sills called the Eagles' treatment of Hurts "very conservative, very patient-focused and appropriately guarded in every step."

This week's news prompted rampant speculation about why the Eagles allowed Hurts to play in London.

Jeff Miller, NFL executive vice president overseeing player health and safety, called such speculation "considerable and uninformed," as well as "unfounded."

"Conservative steps were taken to ensure Jalen Hurts' health was always made the first priority and continues to be," Miller said.

The NFL declined to discuss specifics of Hurts' case, citing medical privacy. But Sills, who has been a team physical for three decades, said he has "tremendous confidence" in the Eagles' medical staff. The NFL works one to two years in advance of international games to prep for medical care, identifying local hospitals, physicians and resources at every site.

The medical experts tasked with evaluating players in such cases are not influenced by the team, Sills said.

"There is no doctor who is taking orders from a football person, a non-medical person. Period," Sills said.

Doctors speculating online about "what should have been done" without all the data or being in the room with a patient are "unprofessional and unethical" in doing so, Sills said, citing a "sacred trust" between physicians and patients.

The NFL has tracked blood clot cases every season for the last decade and shares the data with the NFLPA, Sills said. Each year features a handful of cases.

"This isn't really a new situation, but it's something we examine," Sills said.

The threshold for people flying with superficial blood clots, which Hurts did on the way home from London, depends on the "nuances of each situation," Sills said, adding that the NFL spends significant time planning for player safety as it relates to long flights for international play.

articles.title: Was last Sunday Davante Adams last game with the Rams?
articles.summary: Davante Adams could be back in six weeks, he could basically miss the rest of the season
articles.body:
As Davante Adams hits injured reserved for an expected 6-10 weeks , it's fair to wonder if he suits up for the Los Angeles Rams again? If Adams' recovery takes the full 10 weeks, that puts the Rams in Week 16 or 17. If the Rams haven't turned their season around , what is the point of Adams suiting up for a meaningless game?

If Adams can come back this year, that's very exciting for him and the Rams. Still, how healthy will he be? How hindered or recovered will he be from his ruptured hamstring?

The 33-year-old Adams was on a nice pace for L.A. in 2026 with 480 yards and four touchdowns, but his injury puts him at risk of basically missing the rest of the season, and missing his remaining time with the Rams.

Adams hits free agency in 2027. Unless a new deal is worked out, or unless Adams comes back and plays in 2026, then Adams' last game with the Rams was this past Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals.

It would be a disappointing end to his tenure in L.A.

As far as where Adams goes from here, it will depend on his recovery, if he still wants to play and if a team would be interested. Then there is the contract to work out. The future of Adams in the NFL isn't certain.

Adams was signed as a missing piece to the offense in 2025 and he was. He scored 19 touchdowns his regular seasons and postseason combined after joining up with Sean McVay and Matthew Stafford.

Adams was/is past his prime, and he still was (is?) very good for McVay and the Rams. He came in to functionally replace Cooper Kupp as a veteran wide receiver who could produce, and he did that.

He added to his Hall of Fame resume when he led the NFL with 14 receiving scores in 2025.

But Adams came to L.A. to win a Super Bowl , and that doesn't look likely to happen. As of October 2026, the Rams sit at 2-4 with a real chance to miss the playoffs .

Funnily enough, Kupp won the Super Bowl in 2025 with the Seattle Seahawks. Not Adams. Six weeks into 2026 and another NFC West team is vying for the Super Bowl, but it's the San Francisco 49ers, not the Rams.

Was Adams time in L.A. a success? Yes. Did his time in L.A. deliver what he and the Rams wanted? Unless they win the Super Bowl in 2026, then not exactly.

Adams has been to the NFC Championship Game five times, but the Super Bowl zero. Five NFC Championship losses are both something to be disappointed in, and something to be proud of. Will Adams get the chance to reach a sixth? Unless something changes, it won't be with the Rams. That ship may have sailed , and his time playing days for the Rams, may be behind him.

articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs could miss out on Tyreek Hill as the Los Angeles Rams emerge as a potential destination for the free-agent wide receiver. Kansas City has reasons to consider bringing back its former star after injuries hit its receiving corps, but the Rams have an urgent need of their own. Los Angeles lost Davante Adams to a ruptured hamstring, leaving a major gap in its passing attack. Bleacher Report’s Alex Kay believes the Rams could move for Hill, putting the Chiefs’ reunion hopes in doubt as both teams assess their options.The Rams could move ahead of the Chiefs for Tyreek HillTyreek Hill’s possible move to Los Angeles is tied to Adams’ injury and the Rams’ need to keep their offense competitive. Adams had caught 30 passes for 480 yards and four touchdowns through six games before the hamstring injury threatened to sideline him for an extended stretch.Kay believes Hill could help fill that void if he is ready to return. In his assessment, the former Chiefs and Dolphins receiver offers a level of speed and playmaking that few available free agents can match.“With Adams expected to miss six to 10 weeks while he recovers from a ruptured hamstring, the Rams need to offset the loss of their star wideout with a pickup on the open market,” Kay wrote. “No free agent can move the needle more than Tyreek Hill.”Hill is working his way back from a serious knee injury suffered during the 2025 season. His agent, Drew Rosenhaus, has indicated that the receiver is getting closer to a return, but medical clearance and game readiness remain key questions.Kay also acknowledged the risk involved in signing him. “Hill’s résumé makes him an intriguing potential replacement, although his recovery and lengthy absence create uncertainty about how quickly he could contribute,” Kay wrote.For Los Angeles, the decision comes down to whether Hill can contribute quickly enough to justify the move. The Rams need help now, but signing a receiver returning from a major injury is no guarantee of an immediate fix.The Chiefs may look beyond their former starKansas City has its own reasons to pursue Hill. Injuries to Tyquan Thornton and Rashee Rice have put added pressure on the receiving group, and a familiar face could offer Patrick Mahomes another explosive option.Still, Hill is not the only route available. ESPN analyst Benjamin Solak has suggested the Chiefs could explore a move for Dallas Cowboys receiver George Pickens, whose future in Dallas could become complicated by contract decisions.“His effort level and focus seem to be waning again, and the Cowboys will struggle to pay Pickens and cornerback Joey Porter Jr., whom they recently traded for,” Solak wrote.Solak also outlined a possible trade scenario if Dallas continues to struggle.“If the 2-4 Cowboys keep losing games, I’d call Pickens on the franchise tag for the remainder of the season — we know he has game-breaking ability when he’s dialed in. Imagine Pickens in Los Angeles to help replace Davante Adams … or in Kansas City as Mahomes’ new downfield target? Exciting stuff.”That leaves Kansas City weighing a reunion against other ways to strengthen its offense. Hill’s history with the Chiefs makes the possibility appealing, but Los Angeles has a clear opening following Adams’ injury. articles.title: Diego Pavia Reveals UFL Contract Talks, CFB Star Eyes Comeback After Ravens Exit Before NFL Season
articles.summary: Diego Pavia's next chapter in football will potentially be coming in the UFL.
articles.body:
Diego Pavia's next chapter in football will potentially be coming in the UFL.

The former Vanderbilt quarterback posted on social media Monday that he's currently in negotiations to join the league:

Pavia, 24, went undrafted out of college but signed with the Baltimore Ravens. He didn't last long with the team, however, as the Ravens cut him in late July, one day before rookies were scheduled to report to training camp.

Pavia also spoke on failing to stick with an NFL team and his next steps during an interview with Darius Sanders.

"Super thankful to the Ravens for giving me a chance. No one else did. They were the only team to call after the draft," he said (6:13 mark). "I feel like I've had a few hiccups in my career, maybe what they didn't want to see. But at the end of the day everyone's having fun, everyone's going out, it's just my s--t got televised. ... I'm thankful for what I've been through. My journey is not done. I plan on doing some UFL. If everything goes smooth, I'm planning on bringing some teammates with me. And besides that, man, I'm here to support guys around the world. If they need help, they can reach out to me. I'll be at a lot of games. So, I'm just here to have fun."

Pavia certainly appeared to be having fun out on the field during his time with Vanderbilt, throwing for 5,832 yards, 49 touchdowns and 12 interceptions across two seasons while rushing for 1,663 yards and another 18 scores.

That included last season's impressive 10-3 campaign, Vandy's first 10-win season in school history. And that's a long history—the Commodores began playing football in 1890. While Vanderbilt just missed out on the College Football Playoff, it was a historic season nonetheless.

Without Pavia the Commodores have gone 3-4 this season, losers of four straight. And for fans itching to see him out on the field again, it appears that he has the UFL in his sights.

articles.title: Brock Purdy's story is 'Tom Brady plus a thousand' and deserves NFL spotlight after making history, says Neil Reynolds
articles.summary: Brock Purdy became the highest-rated passer in NFL history as he guided the San Francisco 49ers to victory over the Washington Commanders on Monday night; Sky Sports NFL's Neil Reynolds explores his rise from Mr Irrelevant to NFL superstar as he continues his Super Bowl challenge
articles.body:
You might think it's Aaron Rodgers, Peyton Manning, what about the great Dan Marino, or John Elway? Joe Montana won four Super Bowls, never lost a Super Bowl, surely it's Joe Montana, or what about the GOAT, Tom Brady?

The answer would be no to all of those players, legends though they are.

The highest-rated quarterback in NFL history is Brock Purdy of the San Francisco 49ers. During Monday's victory over the Washington Commanders, he took his career passer rating to 105.6, above every other legend ever to have played the game.

More importantly, Purdy took the 49ers to a 6-0 start and they are in control of the NFC West. How does this happen with a man who was picked last in the 2022 NFL Draft? Mr Irrelevant, overlooked by every NFL team time and time again.

It's Tom Brady plus a thousand in terms of being overlooked and disrespected and, like Brady, Purdy has responded brilliantly in the pros.

I still don't think he gets the respect he deserves because of that label that was attached to him as a low-round draft pick but he's already taken this team to an NFC Championship game, he's taken this team to a Super Bowl and now here he is playing excellent football at the start of the 2026 season.

I've had the opportunity to interview Purdy now three or four times and he's one of the nicest guys you'll ever meet. He's so friendly, so down to earth.

One occasion we interviewed in training camp in San Francisco and they were doing some work on the stadium and every time he answered a question a guy in the background started drilling and that was absolutely nothing to do with Brock Purdy. And yet he apologised profusely and said that he couldn't feel worse.

We met and chatted at the Super Bowl and that's where I found out that the nice guy has a steel running through him. Purdy made note of the fact that he was mocked and ridiculed for being Mr Irrelevant.

Yes he played along with all of the necessary events that go with that position but he kind of kept receipts and he went into that Super Bowl hoping those people who mocked him were going to be sitting in the stands that day as he almost led the 49ers to victory over the Kansas City Chiefs. In fact, he would have been a Super Bowl champion had the NFL not changed its overtime rules.

Purdy is a supercomputer at the quarterback position. He processes quickly, he's accurate and he doesn't need to have an absolute cannon for an arm. Yes he's helped out by Kyle Shanahan with excellent play calling but so was Joe Montana with Bill Walsh, Dan Marino with Don Shula, Jim Kelly with Marv Levy.

All great quarterbacks have a head coach in their corner. It helps this season that Purdy's only been sacked twice and he's already completed 70 per cent of his passes, 14 touchdowns to just two interceptions.

He is unassuming but ruthless and I think the way he spreads the ball around in San Francisco's attack is not only critical to his success so far, I think it's going to really guide this team moving forward.

I'll tell you one last thing on Brock Purdy which I noticed when I watched him in the flesh in Pittsburgh in Week One of the 2023 season. He scrambled off the spot and threw a touchdown pass into the front corner of the end zone, which showed great athleticism. If that had been Steve Young back in the 1990s we would have been lauding that play at every possible opportunity.

Again we don't see Purdy as an athlete but he is. Look at a big touchdown run he had a couple of weeks ago which got called back for a George Kittle holding penalty. Purdy can score from anywhere on the field with his arm, thanks to his brain, but also he can use his legs.

This player who was the last picked in the 2022 NFL Draft is now one of the best in the NFL and he deserves his moment in the spotlight as the highest rated quarterback this league has ever seen.

articles.title: NFL: Players union calls for investigation into Jalen Hurts' medical care after league doctor defends treatment
articles.summary: The NFLPA has called for an investigation into the medical care of Jalen Hurts after the  Philadelphia Eagles quarterback was diagnosed with blood clots before playing against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London; the NFL's doctor, Allen Sills, has defended the Eagles' treatment of Hurts
articles.body:
Reports by The Associated Press suggest that the Eagles will not be disciplined for their actions with Hurts even after NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that the former Super Bowl MVP was in hospital until 4am and did not sleep prior to Philadelphia's defeat to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London.

Hurts, who flew back from London and continued training before further tests ruled him out of the Eagles' most recent game against Carolina, has been ruled out for the rest of the season after being diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli.

Dr Allen Sills, the NFL's chief medical officer, offered a passionate defence of how the Eagles treated Hurts, following a statement from the league that said officials had been in contact with Philadelphia's medical personnel and the Cleveland Clinic in London throughout the process.

"I have complete confidence in the Eagles' medical staff and their handling of this situation, and I would characterise their work as very conservative, very patient-focused and appropriately guarded at every step," Sills said at the league's annual fall meeting. "I don't think you can take that outcome and say there was something flawed about the process. Sometimes in medicine, we do all the right things and diseases progress and other things develop.

"In this case, everyone was incredibly conservative and incredibly vigilant and was very quick to make diagnoses of these conditions that might not have been diagnosed in a nonathlete."

The NFL Players Association said it was told by the league that a review was not planned.

"Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred," the union said. "Determining the facts is essential to ensuring players receive the highest level of care and protection going forward."

NFL executive vice president Jeff Miller took issue with "uninformed speculation" in reports Monday that Hurts went more than 30 hours without sleep last weekend before playing.

"Jalen Hurts returned to the hotel, slept for a period of time and went to the stadium," Miller said, estimating that Hurts slept for around seven or eight hours. "Both talking to the Eagles' staff and making sure from people on the ground, tracking the case, talking to the independent hospital and doctors involved that we have, I think, a complete understanding of the course of events."

Sills said the league and the players' union study and track blood clots annually. He declined to go into specifics about Hurts' condition, citing patient privacy, and reiterated multiple times that treating a blood clot involves looking at multiple factors.

Dr Caron Rockman, a vascular surgeon for roughly 30 years, said based on what she has read, there's no evidence the Eagles acted improperly while dealing with what she called not a textbook issue.

"It's a judgment call," said Rockman, who is currently a chair at Hackensack University Medical Center in New Jersey and did not treat Hurts. "I think it's really a case-by-case basis. In my personal opinion, superficial vein thrombosis is not a (disqualification) to fly."

Hurts' treatment moving forward involves blood thinners, and he will not be allowed to participate in any football activities until he is off them.

The quarterback played in London against Jacksonville on Oct. 11, three days after informing medical staff of the injury after practice. He was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis.

"I think there was incredible vigilance, there was conservative care, state-of-the-art imaging that was done in London," Sills said. "And, as far as the timing and the decision-making, I have great confidence in that and believe that everyone acted with an abundance of caution."

Sills in his opening statement that lasted more than five minutes said all decisions are made with medicine over football.

"The notion that there are external factors or that any of our physicians would put a player in harm's way - that's nonsense," Sills said.

articles.body:
We will start by looking at how Andrew Berry's position room has been built to start the season each year:

2020 - Bitonio, Teller 2021 - Bitonio, Teller, Dunn, Hance 2022 - Bitonio, Teller, Dunn, Froholdt 2023 - Bitonio, Teller 2024 - Bitonio, Teller, Zinter, Cohen 2025 - Bitonio, Teller, Jenkins, Zinter 2026 - Johnson, Jenkins, Zinter

Here is the cash they have spend on the position room and the % of the salary cap:

2020 - $19,774,648 (9.98%) 2021 - $35,336,269 (17.39%) 2022 - $23,929,260 (11.49%) 2023 - $31,439,972 (13.99%) 2024 - $38,700,720 (15.15%) 2025 - $40,935,670 (14.66%) 2026 - $38,701,516 (12.85%)

This looks at the cash in each players contracts and the amount of guarantees they have in their deals:

Zion Johnson 2026 - $18,825,000 (fully guaranteed) 2027 - $14,175,000 ($13,565,000 guaranteed) 2028 - $16,500,000 (no guarantees)

Teven Jenkins 2026 - $4,000,000 (fully guaranteed)

Zak Zinter 2026 - $1,316,340 (no guarantees) 2027 - $1,577,010 (no guarantees)

Here is a look at the list of current unrestricted free agents sorted by the amount of snaps they have played so far this season:

This chart shows the ages of the draft class at the time of the draft. Greens signifies the age of 66% of the prospects they have drafted in this range, yellow 33% and red is an age they have never taken in this range. So while it is unlikely they select a red player, it isn't impossible.

OBR VIP's can see my full October draft board with each position on it here .

I was skeptical when they signed Zion Johnson to a $16.5m a year deal, while you always overpay for early free agency moves, it felt like a significant overpay. He hadn't produced enough in his first four years to be the 16th highest paid guard in the league. But had remained healthy playing over 1,000 snaps each season and was an incredibly athletic player. It feels like they have started to unlock his talent as the season goes along. I expect him to be here in 2027 and if performances remain strong then much longer term. He is turning 27 next month so he could be a two contract player in Cleveland.

Austin Barber made the 53 man roster as a tackle this season. Due to injury he got the chance to push inside to guard and hasn't looked back since. There have been better and worse games but that is to be expected from any rookie. Overall the performances have been strong and he should keep improving. I expect him to remain as a guard long term. They appear to be settled along the majority of the line, so why make a second year player learn to reposition, rather than keep focusing on improving

Teven Jenkins is an incredibly talented player, arguably a top 16 guard in the NFL. The issue is injuries have derailed his entire career. There were questions of would he break $15m a year as a guard when leaving the Bears but the medical must have spooked teams to only get $3m and from Cleveland with two veteran starters ahead of him. He is now six weeks on the injury list, if the team knew he was out that long he would have gone to IR. So signs point to a much slower than expected return. It is a shame as he could be one of the best depth pieces in the league still but availability is the best ability. It wouldn't shock me to see him moved on from during or after the season. Unless he signs again but on a veteran minimum deal this time, battling to make the roster next season.

The expectation was for Zak Zinter was for him to be waived during the cut to 53 players. Monken spoke about being impressed by his play in camp to keep him around. I'm not sure it will be enough to keep him on the roster but he will likely get the chance to compete at camp next year.

I believe they will look to draft someone on day three. While you don't expect to see that play in 2027, you can start developing someone for the future. It is better to use the depth to see if someone can play for the future and build into a position of more strength. If the rookie turns out to be good, it gives you the option to move on if Johnson struggles for some reason in 2027 or they want to move Barber to right tackle for the 2028 season and move on from Howard. Options for the roster or good depth are both beneficial. If the rookie struggles in 2027 during practice, they can always add someone else the year after in the draft to keep searching for depth.

While Jenkins and Zinter might return for training camp in 2027, I would be looking at adding a cheap veteran free agent who can give them injury cover as well as adding a UDFA. This way five players can compete for the one or two depth spots on the roster behind the starters. Andrew Berry has always pushed for extra options so that you can make the best decisions possible for the final 53 as well as having some injury cover.

articles.title: ‘It’s Absolutely Unacceptable’ — Russell Wilson Holds Jayden Daniels and Commanders OC David Blough Accountable for Costly Mistake in Week 6
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders have struggled to manage crucial moments in consecutive games, leaving little room for error as they try to stay competitive. Their...
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders have struggled to manage crucial moments in consecutive games, leaving little room for error as they try to stay competitive. Their offensive execution has come under scrutiny, but the bigger concern involves decisions that have cost them chances to win.

The latest setback against the San Francisco 49ers has prompted questions about communication between the coaching staff and the quarterback.

Now, Super Bowl champion Russell Wilson has weighed in on the mistakes, pointing to two people who must take responsibility for preventing them.

Russell Wilson Calls Out Jayden Daniels, David Blough for Week 6 Mistake

Speaking on the "Set, Hut!" show with former offensive lineman Kyle Long, Wilson criticized the Commanders' handling of a crucial fourth-down situation against San Francisco.

Quarterback Jayden Daniels threw the ball out of bounds under pressure instead of finding an open receiver on a short route, ending the possession without a score.

Long explained that an available option existed near the first-down marker, but pressure from the left forced Daniels to move right. The quarterback ultimately threw the ball away, while sideline footage appeared to show coach Dan Quinn trying to communicate with his team.

Wilson made clear that the responsibility extended beyond Daniels to offensive coordinator David Blough and the coaching staff.

"It's absolutely unacceptable," Wilson said, stressing the importance of understanding the game situation. "The quarterback's got to know the situation, the offensive coordinator's got to know the situation. Obviously, the head coach has to know the situation."

Wilson acknowledged that head coaches can become occupied with other responsibilities during a game. However, he argued that the quarterback and offensive coordinator must recognize the down, distance, and available options before making a decision. He also pointed out that even legendary quarterback Tom Brady once made a similar mistake in Chicago.

Still, Wilson drew a clear distinction between an isolated lapse and Washington's repeated problems. "The reality is that it can't happen two weeks in a row," Wilson said.

Commanders' Clock Management Mistake Raises Concerns

Washington's loss to San Francisco followed another costly mistake against the New York Giants in Week 5.

During overtime of a 27-27 tie, Daniels scrambled with 12 seconds remaining and no timeouts, allowing the clock to expire before Washington could attempt a game-winning field goal.

Wilson connected that missed opportunity to the Commanders' latest defeat. Washington lost 23-17 to the 49ers, and the points left on the field became especially important as the game progressed.

Wilson noted that Washington later failed to convert another fourth-and-8 attempt after taking a sack. Had the Commanders secured points from their earlier opportunities, they could have put themselves in position to win after getting the ball back late.

"They did a great job coming back," Wilson said, crediting Washington's fight despite the mistakes.
